findings.mechanism: BufferPool.free keeps returned buffers for reuse; it is bounded by the peak number of simultaneously live buffers (largest batch, maxBatch=400).
findings.cause: pool high-water mark, not unbounded growth
findings.evidence: Ran 20000 batches via a scratch test (since removed) calling GC and ReadMemStats every 2500 batches. Pool created=400 and idle=400 from batch 2500 on. HeapAlloc stayed flat at ~1.41-1.43 MB. HeapSys plateaued at ~11.8 MB from batch 5000 on.
findings.discriminator: created stops at 400 (= maxBatch) and idle equals created; after warm-up, heap in use and heap reserved from the OS are both flat across 17500 further batches.

findings.mechanism: Renderer.index holds a rendered doc for every invoice in a batch, but RenderBatch deletes every entry and returns the buffers to the pool at the end.
findings.cause: per-batch scratch map, emptied each call
findings.evidence: Code reading, plus the 20000-batch run above where HeapAlloc after GC stayed flat, so entries are not accumulating. Repeated IDs inside a batch Put the old buffer once and replace the entry, so there is no double Put.
findings.discriminator: The map is empty after each RenderBatch (delete loop at batch.go:86-89), and invoice IDs are unique per batch index. Live heap does not grow with the number of batches.
